Query: How does Button Compare to Profound
Response:
Button and Profound are not really direct competitors based on public positioning.

Profound is a GEO / AEO platform. It is built to help brands understand and improve how they appear in AI answers across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Copilot, Meta AI, DeepSeek, and Google AI Overviews. Its public feature set includes Answer Engine Insights, Prompt Volumes, Agent Analytics, AEO/SEO agents, content/brand/PR workflows, sentiment, citations, and AI visibility reporting. 
Profound

Button is a mobile commerce / affiliate / creator-performance platform. Its public messaging focuses on increasing conversions from mobile users, optimizing affiliate and creator commerce journeys, deep linking, machine-learning optimization, app engagement, and revenue per tap. Button says it surpassed $25B in all-time gross merchandise sales, including $10B in 2025, and cites outcomes like higher app installs, revenue per tap, and mobile affiliate revenue. 
Button
 
Button

Bottom line
Dimension	Button	Profound
Core category	Commerce optimization, affiliate, creator, mobile app conversion	AI search visibility, GEO/AEO, LLM brand analytics
Main buyer	Retailers, publishers, creators, advertisers, affiliate teams	Brand, SEO, content, PR, growth, enterprise marketing teams
Main job	Turn traffic/taps into purchases and app conversions	Track and improve brand presence in AI-generated answers
AI use	Optimizes commerce journeys and conversion routing	Measures and influences AI answer visibility, citations, sentiment
Best fit	You already have traffic/creator/affiliate demand and want better monetization	You want to know whether ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini/etc. recommend or cite your brand
My read

Profound is the clearer choice for GEO, AI visibility, and brand presence inside LLM answers. Button is the clearer choice for commerce media, mobile affiliate performance, creator monetization, and conversion optimization.

They could be complementary: Profound helps you get discovered or recommended in AI search; Button helps monetize and optimize downstream commerce journeys once users reach publisher, creator, app, or retail environments.

Query: How does profound compare in the geo market
Response:
As of July 2026, Profound looks like one of the strongest enterprise-oriented players in the GEO/AEO market, especially for brands that want to measure and improve how they appear in AI answers across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Google AI Overviews, and similar surfaces.

Bottom line

Profound is likely a top-tier GEO platform, but not necessarily the best fit for every company. It appears strongest for enterprise marketing, SEO, brand, PR, and demand teams that need robust visibility tracking, competitive intelligence, AI-crawler analytics, prompt demand data, and workflow support for generating AI-search-optimized content. Its own site emphasizes Answer Engine Insights, Agents, Agent Analytics, Aim, prompt volumes, source citations, sentiment, and crawler tracking across major AI engines. 
Profound

For smaller teams, agencies, or companies just starting with AI visibility, tools like OtterlyAI, Peec AI, AthenaHQ, Scrunch, Promptwatch, Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit, Bluefish, AirOps, and Adobe LLM Optimizer may be more practical depending on budget, workflow depth, and whether you need monitoring only or a full optimization system. Comparative vendor pages place Profound among the “leaders,” usually positioned around enterprise analytics plus crawler logs, while competitors often differentiate on usability, content workflows, agency features, or AI-agent delivery. 
Otterly
+1

Where Profound seems strongest

1. Enterprise positioning and funding

Profound has been one of the most visible and best-funded startups in the category. Its Series A announcement said it raised $20 million led by Kleiner Perkins, and Yahoo/Fortune reported a later $96 million round bringing total funding to $155 million. 
Profound
+1
 That does not prove product superiority, but it does suggest strong investor conviction and the ability to build an enterprise sales, support, and product organization.

2. Read + write workflow

Profound is not just a dashboard for “are we mentioned in ChatGPT?” It markets a broader system: measure AI visibility, understand citations and sentiment, track AI bot crawling, identify high-impact work, and use agents to produce AEO/GEO-friendly content. 
Profound
 That makes it more compelling for teams that want to operationalize GEO, not merely report on it.

3. AI-crawler and bot analytics

A big differentiator is Profound’s focus on tracking how sites are interpreted and crawled by AI systems like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity. 
Profound
 In GEO, this matters because visibility is influenced not only by content quality, but also by whether AI systems can discover, retrieve, cite, and trust your content.

4. Enterprise buyer fit

Independent and competitor-authored comparisons consistently position Profound as an enterprise-grade option. One research-based review describes it as “Best for Enterprise,” highlighting prompt-volume demand data and broad engine coverage, while also noting premium pricing and gated access. 
Arfadia
 Scrunch’s comparison similarly says Profound has a broad feature set and is often evaluated by larger teams, while advising buyers to validate complexity and learning curve. 
Scrunch

Where Profound may be weaker

1. It may be overkill for early-stage GEO programs

For a smaller brand, Profound may be more platform than you need. If your immediate goal is basic AI answer monitoring, share-of-voice tracking, and citation checks, lighter tools like OtterlyAI, Peec AI, Promptwatch, or Semrush’s AI visibility products may be easier to start with. Otterly’s own comparison categorizes Profound as a leader but specifically frames it around enterprise analytics and crawler logs. 
Otterly

2. The category is still immature

GEO is evolving fast, and a lot of public comparisons are vendor-authored or SEO-content-driven. Even Scrunch’s buyer guide warns that many AEO/GEO tools look similar on paper and should be validated live in a demo. 
Scrunch
 I would treat any ranking that says “X is the best GEO tool” with caution unless it shows methodology, real test prompts, industries tested, and before/after impact.

3. Optimization impact is hard to prove

Tracking brand mentions is easier than proving causality. The hard question is: did the tool actually improve your inclusion, citations, sentiment, and AI-referred traffic, or did it just measure changes? This is a key diligence area for Profound and every competitor.

Competitive positioning

Profound vs. OtterlyAI / Peec AI: Profound appears more enterprise and workflow-heavy. OtterlyAI and Peec AI look more approachable for monitoring, reporting, and getting started quickly.

Profound vs. Scrunch: Scrunch positions itself as broader end-to-end AEO/GEO, including monitoring, auditing, optimization, and AI-specific content delivery. It lists Profound as a strong broad-feature platform but implies buyers should validate complexity and fit. 
Scrunch

Profound vs. AthenaHQ: AthenaHQ markets itself aggressively against Profound and Peec AI, but its comparisons are self-published, so I would use them as sales material rather than neutral evidence. 
AthenaHQ - Action on AI Search

Profound vs. Semrush / Ahrefs: Semrush and Ahrefs have advantages if your team already lives in traditional SEO workflows. Profound is more purpose-built for AI answer visibility, while SEO suites are still extending into the category.

Profound vs. AirOps / Optiversal: Profound appears more focused on visibility measurement and AEO intelligence, while AirOps and Optiversal are often discussed more around content production and workflow automation. Business Insider reported brands using vendors including Profound, AirOps, and Optiversal as marketers adapt content for AI platforms. 
Business Insider

My take

For a large brand, Profound should be on the shortlist. It is one of the clearest category leaders for enterprise GEO/AEO, especially if you care about competitive visibility, AI crawler behavior, source citations, sentiment, prompt demand, and operational workflows.

For a mid-market company or agency, I would compare Profound against Scrunch, OtterlyAI, Peec AI, Promptwatch, and AthenaHQ before buying. Profound may win on depth, but another tool may win on speed, usability, price, or client reporting.

For a lean startup, Profound may be too heavy unless AI-search visibility is already a major acquisition channel. Start with measurement, identify where AI engines cite competitors, improve authoritative content and third-party mentions, then graduate to a deeper platform when the workflow becomes repeatable.

Query: Is peekai the best observability platform
Response:
PeekAI does not look like the best overall observability platform based on current public information. It looks like a narrow, lightweight, local-first tool rather than a mature, full-featured production observability platform.

There are also two “PeekAI” references that matter:

peekai / Python agent observability library — a local-first, no-cloud debugging tool for Python AI agents. Its PyPI page describes version 0.1.2, released June 21, 2026, with LLM call, tool-use, token, and cost visibility. 
PyPI

peekai.us — appears to be an AI visibility / brand reporting tool that shows how multiple AI platforms describe a brand, not a general AI observability platform. 
Peekai

For LLM / AI app observability, more established options show up repeatedly in current comparisons: Langfuse, LangSmith, Arize Phoenix / Arize, Helicone, Weights & Biases Weave, Braintrust, Datadog LLM Observability, Pydantic Logfire, and Confident AI. Multiple recent comparison pieces frame the market around those tools rather than PeekAI. 
AIpedia
+3
Deepak Gupta
+3
AppScale Blog
+3

My take:

Use case	Better fit
Local-first debugging for a small Python agent project	PeekAI could be a good fit
Open-source LLM observability with tracing, evals, prompt/version workflows	Langfuse
LangChain / LangGraph-heavy apps	LangSmith
Enterprise ML + LLM monitoring	Arize / Phoenix
Fast gateway-style logging and cost tracking	Helicone
Evaluation-driven LLM quality monitoring	Braintrust or Confident AI
Full-stack production app observability	Datadog, New Relic, Pydantic Logfire, or similar

So the honest answer is: PeekAI is probably not “the best observability platform” overall. It may be useful if your priority is simple, local, privacy-friendly observability for Python AI agents, but it does not yet appear to compete head-to-head with the broader production LLM observability platforms.

Query: WHo is the best at optimizing in lLMs for brands
Response:
For brand optimization in LLMs / AI search, the best overall vendor right now appears to be Profound — especially for enterprise brands that want visibility tracking, competitive intelligence, sentiment, citations, and workflows to improve how they show up in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude, and Google AI-style results.

My ranking:

Rank	Platform	Best fit	Why
1	Profound	Enterprise / serious brand GEO programs	Strongest positioning, broad AI-search focus, major funding, and increasingly moving from analytics into execution with “Agents.” Profound says it tracks mentions, sentiment, and performance across major answer engines, and recently announced a $96M Series C at a $1B valuation. 
Profound

2	Peec AI	Growth teams, agencies, mid-market brands	Strong momentum and likely easier entry point than Profound. Peec says it helps teams track visibility, benchmark competitors, and optimize across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini. It also announced 1,300+ brands/agencies onboarded and $4M+ ARR within 10 months. 
Peec AI
+1

3	Semrush / BrightEdge / Adobe-type incumbents	Brands already deeply invested in SEO suites	Safer for companies that want AI visibility layered into existing SEO workflows, but they may be less specialized than AI-native GEO platforms. Semrush describes GEO tools as useful for tracking AI citations, mentions, competitors, and AI search visibility. 
Semrush

4	Lantern / Limy / Azoma / other vertical specialists	E-commerce or agentic shopping use cases	These are interesting if the problem is not just “brand visibility” but “will AI agents recommend or buy my product?” Lantern is focused on e-commerce GEO, while Limy focuses more on AI-agent behavior and attribution. 
Business Insider
+1

Bottom line:
If you are asking “who is best” for a large brand that wants to win in LLM answers, I’d pick Profound. It looks like the category leader for enterprise AI-search visibility and optimization.

If you are a smaller brand, agency, or cost-sensitive team, I’d look hard at Peec AI because its traction is strong and the product seems more accessible.

If you are an e-commerce brand, the answer may not be Profound; I’d also evaluate Lantern, Limy, or Azoma, because product-level recommendation and agentic-shopping visibility are a different problem than broad brand mentions.

One important caveat: this category is still early. Recent research suggests there is no universal optimization recipe; the best strategy depends on whether a brand is a category leader, challenger, mid-market player, or regional/specialist brand.
